  "content": "\"\"\"Known-answer tests for the PBO (CSCV) estimator.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom backtest.factory.pbo import (\n    probability_of_backtest_overfitting as pbo_fn,\n)\n\n\ndef test_dominant_strategy_has_low_pbo():\n    \"\"\"A strategy that genuinely dominates every period generalises OOS -> PBO ~ 0.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)\n    T, N = 200, 8\n    M = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(T, N))\n    M[:, 0] = rng.normal(1.0, 0.4, size=T)  # high, stable Sharpe -> real edge\n    res = pbo_fn(M, n_partitions=10)\n    assert res.pbo < 0.05, f\"dominant strategy should give low PBO, got {res.pbo}\"\n    assert res.median_logit > 0\n\n\ndef test_iid_noise_pbo_near_half():\n    \"\"\"All strategies iid noise -> selection is chance -> PBO ~ 0.5.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)\n    T, N = 240, 12\n    M = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, size=(T, N))\n    res = pbo_fn(M, n_partitions=10)\n    assert 0.3 < res.pbo < 0.7, f\"iid noise PBO should be ~0.5, got {res.pbo}\"\n\n\ndef test_split_count_is_C_S_half():\n    from math import comb\n\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)\n    M = rng.normal(size=(120, 5))\n    res = pbo_fn(M, n_partitions=8)\n    assert res.n_splits == comb(8, 4) == 70\n\n\ndef test_validation_errors():\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        pbo_fn(rng.normal(size=(100, 5)), n_partitions=7)  # odd S\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        pbo_fn(rng.normal(size=(100, 1)), n_partitions=8)  # N < 2\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        pbo_fn(rng.normal(size=(6, 5)), n_partitions=8)  # S > T\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        pbo_fn(rng.normal(size=(100,)), n_partitions=8)  # not 2-D\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"Strategy Card -- the pre-registered hypothesis unit of the discovery factory.\n\nA card commits, BEFORE any backtest, to: what the strategy is, the instruments\nand timeframes its economic rationale actually supports, its default params, the\ngrid to sweep, and -- mandatory -- WHY it should work. Cards with no economic\nrationale are killed at Phase 1 (the anti-p-hacking gate): we do not test\n\"RSI<30 buy\" just because it is mechanically expressible.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nVALID_FAMILIES = {\n    \"trend\",\n    \"meanrev\",\n    \"breakout\",\n    \"relative_value\",\n    \"calendar\",\n    \"breadth\",\n}\n\n# Minimum characters of genuine rationale. A blank or one-word \"momentum\" fails.\nMIN_RATIONALE_CHARS = 25\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass StrategyCard:\n    name: str\n    family: str\n    signal_ref: str  # \"backtest.meanrev_signals:generate_bollinger_rsi_signals\"\n    entry: str\n    exit: str\n    economic_rationale: str\n    native_instruments: list[str]\n    native_timeframes: list[str]\n    default_params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n    param_grid: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # name -> [values]\n    known_failure_modes: str = \"\"\n    prior_verdict: str | None = None\n\n    def problems(self) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Return a list of validation problems; empty list == card passes the gate.\"\"\"\n        problems: list[str] = []\n        if not self.name:\n            problems.append(\"missing name\")\n        if self.family not in VALID_FAMILIES:\n            problems.append(f\"family '{self.family}' not in {sorted(VALID_FAMILIES)}\")\n        if \":\" not in self.signal_ref:\n            problems.append(\"signal_ref must be 'module.path:function'\")\n        if len((self.economic_rationale or \"\").strip()) < MIN_RATIONALE_CHARS:\n            problems.append(\n                f\"economic_rationale too thin (< {MIN_RATIONALE_CHARS} chars) -- \"\n                \"killed by the anti-p-hacking gate\"\n            )\n        if not self.native_instruments:\n            problems.append(\"native_instruments empty\")\n        if not self.native_timeframes:\n            problems.append(\"native_timeframes empty\")\n        return problems\n\n    def is_valid(self) -> bool:\n        return not self.problems()\n\n    def n_param_combos(self) -> int:\n        n = 1\n        for values in self.param_grid.values():\n            n *= max(1, len(values))\n        return n\n\n\ndef save_cards(cards: list[StrategyCard], path: str | Path) -> None:\n    path = Path(path)\n    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    with path.open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        for c in cards:\n            fh.write(json.dumps(asdict(c)) + \"\\n\")\n\n\ndef load_cards(path: str | Path, *, drop_invalid: bool = True) -> list[StrategyCard]:\n    \"\"\"Load cards from jsonl. With drop_invalid, rationale-less cards are silently\n    filtered (the Phase-1 gate); otherwise an invalid card raises.\"\"\"\n    cards: list[StrategyCard] = []\n    with Path(path).open(encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        for line in fh:\n            line = line.strip()\n            if not line:\n                continue\n            card = StrategyCard(**json.loads(line))\n            problems = card.problems()\n            if problems:\n                if drop_invalid:\n                    continue\n                raise ValueError(f\"invalid card '{card.name}': {problems}\")\n            cards.append(card)\n    return cards\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Uniform signal adapter -- one calling convention for every generator.\n\nEach StrategyCard names a signal generator as 'module.path:function'. The\ngenerators already share a contract -- generate_*_signals(df, **params) returns a\nframe carrying the Backtester's required columns -- but they differ in which\noptional columns they fill. This adapter resolves the function, runs it, and\nnormalises the output to exactly what Backtester.run expects, so the funnel can\ntreat all strategies identically.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport importlib\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\n# Backtester.run (engine/backtest/backtester.py) requires these columns.\nREQUIRED_INPUT = [\"open\", \"high\", \"low\", \"close\"]\nREQUIRED_SIGNAL = [\"entry_signal\", \"bias\", \"stop_level\", \"target_1\"]\nFULL_CONTRACT = [\n    \"open\",\n    \"high\",\n    \"low\",\n    \"close\",\n    \"entry_signal\",\n    \"bias\",\n    \"stop_level\",\n    \"target_1\",\n    \"target_2\",\n    \"target_3\",\n    \"regime\",\n    \"exit_signal\",\n]\n\n\ndef resolve_signal_fn(signal_ref: str) -> Callable:\n    \"\"\"'backtest.meanrev_signals:generate_bollinger_rsi_signals' -> the function.\"\"\"\n    module_path, _, func_name = signal_ref.partition(\":\")\n    if not module_path or not func_name:\n        raise ValueError(f\"bad signal_ref '{signal_ref}' (want 'module:function')\")\n    module = importlib.import_module(module_path)\n    return getattr(module, func_name)\n\n\ndef build_signal_frame(\n    signal_ref: str,\n    bars: pd.DataFrame,\n    params: dict,\n) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Run a generator and return a frame satisfying Backtester.run's contract.\n\n    Raises if the generator fails to emit the mandatory signal columns (that means\n    the generator is broken for this input, not something to paper over). Optional\n    columns are backfilled with safe, non-look-ahead defaults.\n    \"\"\"\n    for col in REQUIRED_INPUT:\n        if col not in bars.columns:\n            raise ValueError(f\"input bars missing required column '{col}'\")\n\n    fn = resolve_signal_fn(signal_ref)\n    out = fn(bars.copy(), **params)\n\n    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_SIGNAL if c not in out.columns]\n    if missing:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"generator '{signal_ref}' did not emit required signal columns {missing}\"\n        )\n\n    # Backfill optional columns the Backtester reads via .get() but that some\n    # generators omit. target_2/3 default to target_1 (single-target exit);\n    # regime/exit_signal default to inert values.\n    if \"target_2\" not in out.columns:\n        out[\"target_2\"] = out[\"target_1\"]\n    if \"target_3\" not in out.columns:\n        out[\"target_3\"] = out[\"target_1\"]\n    if \"regime\" not in out.columns:\n        out[\"regime\"] = \"\"\n    if \"exit_signal\" not in out.columns:\n        out[\"exit_signal\"] = \"NO_EXIT\"\n    return out\n"
}
```

  "content": "\"\"\"SQLite results store + global trial counter for the discovery factory.\n\nEvery candidate ever screened is logged here. The global trial counter is the\ndenominator that makes multiple-testing honest: the Deflated Sharpe ratio for\nany survivor must be deflated by the TOTAL number of candidates the factory\nscreened (across all cards/instruments/timeframes), not just one sub-sweep.\nPersisting every candidate also forecloses the \"quietly tested a tiny subset\"\nfailure mode -- the DB is the audit trail.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n_SCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (\n    run_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    config     TEXT NOT NULL\n);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS candidates (\n    candidate_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    run_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    card_name    TEXT NOT NULL,\n    instrument   TEXT NOT NULL,\n    timeframe    TEXT NOT NULL,\n    params       TEXT NOT NULL,\n    stage        TEXT NOT NULL,          -- enumerated | smoke | robustness | combo\n    FOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES runs(run_id)\n);\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS results (\n    result_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    candidate_id INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    stage        TEXT NOT NULL,\n    metrics      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- json\n    verdict      TEXT,                   -- PASS | FAIL | KILL | NULL\n    kill_reason  TEXT,\n    FOREIGN KEY (candidate_id) REFERENCES candidates(candidate_id)\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nclass ResultsDB:\n    def __init__(self, path: str | Path):\n        self.path = str(path)\n        Path(self.path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(self.path)\n        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n        self.conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)\n        self.conn.commit()\n\n    def new_run(self, created_at: str, config: dict) -> int:\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO runs (created_at, config) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n            (created_at, json.dumps(config)),\n        )\n        self.conn.commit()\n        return int(cur.lastrowid)\n\n    def record_candidate(\n        self,\n        run_id: int,\n        card_name: str,\n        instrument: str,\n        timeframe: str,\n        params: dict,\n        stage: str,\n    ) -> int:\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO candidates (run_id, card_name, instrument, timeframe, params, stage)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (run_id, card_name, instrument, timeframe, json.dumps(params), stage),\n        )\n        self.conn.commit()\n        return int(cur.lastrowid)\n\n    def record_result(\n        self,\n        candidate_id: int,\n        stage: str,\n        metrics: dict,\n        verdict: str | None = None,\n        kill_reason: str | None = None,\n    ) -> int:\n        cur = self.conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO results (candidate_id, stage, metrics, verdict, kill_reason)\"\n            \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (candidate_id, stage, json.dumps(metrics), verdict, kill_reason),\n        )\n        self.conn.commit()\n        return int(cur.lastrowid)\n\n    def global_trial_count(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Total candidates ever screened -- the DSR n_trials denominator.\"\"\"\n        row = self.conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM candidates\").fetchone()\n        return int(row[\"n\"])\n\n    def survivors(self, run_id: int, stage: str, verdict: str = \"PASS\") -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Candidates with a given verdict at a given stage.\"\"\"\n        rows = self.conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT c.*, r.metrics, r.verdict, r.kill_reason \"\n            \"FROM candidates c JOIN results r ON r.candidate_id = c.candidate_id \"\n            \"WHERE c.run_id = ? AND r.stage = ? AND r.verdict = ?\",\n            (run_id, stage, verdict),\n        ).fetchall()\n        out = []\n        for row in rows:\n            d = dict(row)\n            d[\"params\"] = json.loads(d[\"params\"])\n            d[\"metrics\"] = json.loads(d[\"metrics\"])\n            out.append(d)\n        return out\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        self.conn.close()\n"
}

===== _find_latest_cache full fn =====
def _find_latest_cache(data_dir: Path, prefix: str, suffix: str = "_1h.csv") -> Path:
    """Pick the cache file whose filename's second date segment is the latest.

    Filename contract (LOAD-BEARING — see ``export_ibkr_history.py``
    ``CACHE_FILENAME_CONTRACT`` for the canonical regex):

        ``<PREFIX>_<START_DATE>_<END_DATE><SUFFIX>``

    where ``<START_DATE>`` and ``<END_DATE>`` are ISO ``YYYY-MM-DD`` strings.
    Lexicographic max on the second underscore-split segment (``parts[2]``,
    the end-date) is equivalent to chronological max because ISO dates sort
    correctly as strings. ``parts[0]`` is the prefix, ``parts[1]`` is the
    start-date, ``parts[2]`` is the end-date — the sort key.

    A refreshed IBKR pull (e.g. ``MES_2024-01-01_2026-05-07_1h.csv``) will
    therefore always win over an older copy (e.g.
    ``MES_2024-01-01_2026-03-28_1h.csv``). Centralizes the bug-class fix from
    commit 55739db so future runners (MES, MGC, MNQ, MCL, M2K, ...) cannot
    silently revert to a hardcoded path.

    Contract drift policy: filenames matching the glob ``<prefix>*<suffix>``
    but violating the underscore-split contract (fewer than 3 segments) sort
    to the empty string and end up at the bottom of the lex order, so they
    never beat a contract-conforming sibling. They will only be selected if
    no conforming file exists, in which case the helper falls back to the
    glob-sort tail and a warning is logged. The companion runtime assertion
    in ``export_ibkr_history._save_merged`` is the canary that prevents new
    drift from entering the cache directory.

    Args:
        data_dir: Directory to search (typically ``engine/backtest/cache/``).

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""
3	MES ORB Gate v2 — Rank 1 Verdict
4	
5	Opening Range Breakout strategy for MES (Micro E-mini S&P 500).
6	
7	Strategy:
8	    Opening Range = high/low of the first RTH bar (09:30-10:30 ET on 1h data).
9	    LONG entry when price closes above OR High (upside breakout).
10	    SHORT entry when price closes below OR Low (downside breakout).
11	    Stop: opposite side of OR. T1: 1x OR range extension. T2: 2x.
12	    Partial exit: 50% at T1 (stop moves to breakeven), 50% at T2 or EOD.
13	    EOD: any open position force-closed at 15:xx bar close.
14	
15	Why MES ORB has the highest prior probability of any unexplored strategy:
16	    Per session 6 analysis, MES has the most favorable stop geometry of any
17	    instrument in the portfolio:
18	      - MES ATR(14): typically 12-25 S&P points
19	      - MES OR range at 0.08% threshold: ~6-10 points
20	      - ATR/OR_range ratio: 2-3x (stop is meaningfully tighter than typical noise)
21	    Compare to MNQ ORB (FAIL): ATR/OR_range = 5-8x, stops blown by routine vol.
22	    The MES SMA trend rank11 PASS already validates that MES has tradeable
23	    structure on 1h bars — ORB tests a complementary intraday timing pattern.
24	
25	Why ORB avoids the SMA scarcity problem:
26	    SMA crossovers fire 3-18x per year on MES — sometimes too few for clean OOS.
27	    ORB fires ~1-2x per RTH day (~21-42 per 1-month OOS window). Gate v2
28	    statistical tests become meaningful immediately.
29	
30	Parameter grid (16 combos = 2x2x4):
31	    volume_filter:    [True, False]   - require vol >= 80% of 20-bar avg on breakout
32	    regime_filter:    [False, True]   - block entries in EXHAUSTED/COMPRESSION regime
33	    min_or_range_pct: [0.0005, 0.0008, 0.0012, 0.0015]  - min OR range as % of price

35	MES contract specs:
36	    multiplier : $5.0/point  (Micro E-mini S&P 500)

38	    commission : $0.62/contract/side (IB Tiered micro)

129	def _load_data(data_file: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
130	    df = pd.read_csv(data_file)
131	    df.columns = [c.lower() for c in df.columns]
132	    ts_col = "timestamp" if "timestamp" in df.columns else "datetime"
133	    # IBKR cache timestamps are naive UTC. orb_signals.py expects Eastern Time
134	    # (hour==9 for RTH open bar). Localize then convert so _detect_rth_open_bar()
135	    # finds the correct 09:00-10:00 ET bar (13:00 UTC during EDT, 14:00 during EST).
136	    ts = pd.to_datetime(df[ts_col])
137	    if ts.dt.tz is None:
138	        ts = ts.dt.tz_localize("UTC").dt.tz_convert("America/New_York")
139	    df[ts_col] = ts
140	    df = df.set_index(ts_col).sort_index()
141	    required = {"open", "high", "low", "close"}
142	    missing = required - set(df.columns)
143	    if missing:
144	        raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in {data_file.name}: {missing}")
145	    return df

161	
162	def _generate_windows(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
163	    data_start = df.index.min()
164	    data_end = df.index.max()
165	    windows = []
166	    cursor = data_start
167	    wnum = 1
168	    while True:
169	        train_start = cursor
170	        train_end = train_start + pd.DateOffset(months=TRAIN_MONTHS)
171	        test_start = train_end
172	        test_end = test_start + pd.DateOffset(months=TEST_MONTHS)
173	        if test_start >= data_end:
174	            break
175	        if test_end > data_end:
176	            test_end = data_end
177	        df_train = df[(df.index >= train_start) & (df.index < train_end)]
178	        df_test = df[(df.index >= test_start) & (df.index <= test_end)]
179	        if len(df_train) >= 30 and len(df_test) >= 30:
180	            windows.append(
181	                {
182	                    "window_num": wnum,
183	                    "train_start": train_start,
184	                    "train_end": train_end,
185	                    "test_start": test_start,
186	                    "test_end": test_end,
187	                    "n_train": len(df_train),
188	                    "n_test": len(df_test),
189	                }
190	            )
191	            wnum += 1
192	        cursor += pd.DateOffset(months=STEP_MONTHS)
193	        if cursor >= data_end:
194	            break
195	    return windows

240	def _best_is_params(df_train: pd.DataFrame, grid: list[tuple]) -> tuple:
241	    best_score = -1.0
242	    best_params = None
243	    best_result = None
244	
245	    for vol_f, reg_f, min_or in grid:
246	        try:
247	            r = _run_orb(df_train, vol_f, reg_f, min_or)
248	        except Exception as exc:
249	            print(f"    [WARN] IS error (vol={vol_f}, reg={reg_f}, or={min_or}): {exc}")
250	            continue
251	        if r.total_trades < MIN_OOS_TRADES_PER_WINDOW:
252	            continue
253	        # Score: profit factor (capped at 5 to prevent inf domination)
254	        pf_capped = min(r.profit_factor, 5.0) if r.profit_factor != float("inf") else 5.0
255	        score = pf_capped
256	        if score > best_score:
257	            best_score = score
258	            best_params = {
259	                "volume_filter": vol_f,
260	                "regime_filter": reg_f,
261	                "min_or_range_pct": min_or,
262	            }
263	            best_result = r
264	
265	    return best_params, best_result

372	            )

375	        except Exception as exc:

385	
386	
387	def _compute_gate_v2(
388	    oos_results: list,
389	    n_grid_combos: int,
390	    fixed_params_metrics: dict,
391	    cost_sweep_metrics: dict,
392	) -> dict:
393	    from backtest.deflated_sharpe import deflated_sharpe_ratio
394	
395	    oos_pfs = [r.profit_factor for r in oos_results if r.total_trades >= MIN_OOS_TRADES_PER_WINDOW]
396	    oos_dds = [r.max_drawdown_pct for r in oos_results]
397	    oos_sharpes = [
398	        r.sharpe_ratio for r in oos_results if r.total_trades >= MIN_OOS_TRADES_PER_WINDOW
399	    ]
400	    all_trades = sum(r.total_trades for r in oos_results)
401	
402	    pf_ci_lower = _bootstrap_pf_ci_lower(oos_pfs)
403	    p_edge = float(sum(1 for pf in oos_pfs if pf > 1.0) / max(1, len(oos_pfs)))
404	    mc_95th_dd = float(np.percentile(oos_dds, 95.0)) if oos_dds else 1.0
405	    mean_sharpe = float(np.mean(oos_sharpes)) if oos_sharpes else 0.0
406	    n_obs = max(all_trades, 30)
407	    dsr_result = deflated_sharpe_ratio(sharpe=mean_sharpe, n_trials=n_grid_combos, n_obs=n_obs)
408	    dsr = dsr_result.get("dsr", 0.0) if isinstance(dsr_result, dict) else float(dsr_result)
409	
410	    wfo_consistency = _classify_wfo_consistency(oos_pfs)
411	    fixed_params_min_pf = fixed_params_metrics.get("fixed_params_min_pf", 0.0)
412	    cost_survives_through = cost_sweep_metrics.get("cost_survives_through", "none")
413	    cost_tier_idx = (
414	        COST_TIER_ORDER.index(cost_survives_through)
415	        if cost_survives_through in COST_TIER_ORDER
416	        else -1
417	    )
418	    cost_realistic_idx = COST_TIER_ORDER.index("realistic")
419	    cost_passes = cost_tier_idx >= cost_realistic_idx
420	
421	    core_pass = (
422	        pf_ci_lower >= GATE_PF_CI_LOWER
423	        and p_edge >= GATE_P_EDGE
424	        and mc_95th_dd <= GATE_MC_DD_CORE
425	        and dsr >= GATE_DSR
426	    )
427	    alt_pass = (
428	        dsr >= GATE_DSR_ALT
429	        and wfo_consistency in GATE_WFO_CONSISTENCY_VALUES
430	        and fixed_params_min_pf >= GATE_FIXED_PARAMS_MIN_PF
431	        and cost_passes
432	        and mc_95th_dd <= GATE_MC_DD_ALT
433	    )
434	
435	    def _cr(label, val, threshold, op):
436	        passed = (val >= threshold) if op == ">=" else (val <= threshold)
437	        prefix = "" if passed else "FAIL "
438	        return f"{prefix}{label}={val:.4f} {op} {threshold}"
439

  "new_string": "def _intraday(start: str = \"2024-01-01\", end: str = \"2025-04-01\", freq: str = \"4h\", seed: int = 7) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Span real calendar time (so >=4 WFO windows form) at a coarse intraday freq\n    (so the event-loop backtester stays fast).\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    idx = pd.date_range(start, end, freq=freq, tz=\"America/New_York\")\n    n = len(idx)\n    drift = np.linspace(0, 8, n)\n    noise = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.4, n))\n    close = 100 + drift + noise\n    high = close + np.abs(rng.normal(0, 0.3, n))\n    low = close - np.abs(rng.normal(0, 0.3, n))\n    return pd.DataFrame({\"open\": close, \"high\": high, \"low\": low, \"close\": close}, index=idx)\n\n\ndef _thin(months: int = 2, seed: int = 7) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    n = months * 120\n    idx = pd.date_range(\"2024-01-01\", periods=n, freq=\"4h\", tz=\"America/New_York\")\n    close = 100 + np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.4, n))\n    return pd.DataFrame(\n        {\"open\": close, \"high\": close + 0.3, \"low\": close - 0.3, \"close\": close}, index=idx\n    )"

170	        FileNotFoundError: If no files match ``<prefix>*<suffix>`` in ``data_dir``.
171	    """
172	    import logging
173	
174	    # Anchor the symbol on a trailing underscore so a prefix like "MES" matches
175	    # "MES_2024-..._1h.csv" but NOT a longer symbol that merely starts with it
176	    # ("MESXX_..._1h.csv"). The filename contract is <SYMBOL>_<START>_<END>_<INTERVAL>,
177	    # so a "_" always follows the symbol. Without the anchor, glob "MES*" leaks
178	    # MESXX files into MES's candidate set and a same-end-date tie can silently
179	    # select the wrong symbol's cache.
180	    candidates = sorted(data_dir.glob(f"{prefix}_*{suffix}"))
181	    if not candidates:
182	        raise FileNotFoundError(
183	            f"No {prefix} {suffix.lstrip('_').rstrip('.csv')} data found in "
184	            f"{data_dir} (looked for '{prefix}_*{suffix}')"
185	        )
186	
187	    def _end_date(p: Path) -> str:
188	        # Filename: <PREFIX>_YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD<SUFFIX> -> the second date.
189	        # Off-contract files have <3 parts and return "" (sort to the bottom).
190	        parts = p.stem.split("_")
191	        return parts[2] if len(parts) >= 3 else ""
192	
193	    # Surface contract-violating files so drift is visible in logs.
194	    off_contract = [p for p in candidates if not _end_date(p)]
195	    if off_contract:
196	        logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(
197	            "Cache filename contract drift detected in %s: %s "
198	            "(expected '<PREFIX>_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<YYYY-MM-DD>%s')",
199	            data_dir,
200	            [p.name for p in off_contract],
201	            suffix,
202	        )
203	
204	    return max(candidates, key=_end_date)
205	
206	
207	def bootstrap_pf_ci_lower(oos_pfs: list[float], n: int = 5000) -> float:
208	    """Bootstrap 5th-percentile of mean PF distribution; inf-cap baked in."""
209	    # Cap inf/-inf before bootstrapping — np.percentile returns NaN via inf-inf interpolation
210	    capped = [
211	        (
212	            min(max(pf, 0.0), 5.0)
213	            if not (pf == float("inf") or pf == float("-inf"))
214	            else (5.0 if pf == float("inf") else 0.0)
215	        )
216	        for pf in oos_pfs
217	    ]
218	    if len(capped) < 2:
219	        return float(np.mean(capped)) if capped else 0.0
220	    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
221	    arr = np.array(capped, dtype=float)
222	    boot_means = [rng.choice(arr, size=len(arr), replace=True).mean() for _ in range(n)]
223	    return float(np.percentile(boot_means, 5.0))
224

371	def compute_gate_v2(
372	    oos_results: list[OOSResult],
373	    n_grid_combos: int,
374	    fixed_params_metrics: dict,
375	    cost_sweep_metrics: dict,
376	    min_trades: int = 1,
377	) -> dict:
378	    """Compute gate v2 PASS/FAIL from OOS results and auxiliary sweep outputs.
379	
380	    Implements the dual-path (core + ALT) decision logic extracted from every
381	    runner's private _compute_gate_v2 function. Functionally identical to those
382	    copies.
383	
384	    Core path:  pf_ci_lower >= 1.10
385	                AND p_edge >= 0.95
386	                AND mc_95th_dd <= 5%
387	                AND dsr >= 0.10
388	
389	    ALT path:   dsr >= 0.30
390	                AND wfo_consistency in [MODERATE, STRONG]
391	                AND fixed_params_min_pf >= 1.20
392	                AND cost_survives_through >= realistic
393	                AND mc_95th_dd <= 4%
394	    """
395	    from backtest.deflated_sharpe import deflated_sharpe_ratio
396	
397	    qualified = [r for r in oos_results if r.total_trades >= min_trades]
398	    oos_pfs = [r.profit_factor for r in qualified]
399	    oos_dds = [r.max_drawdown_pct for r in oos_results]
400	    oos_sharpes = [r.sharpe_ratio for r in qualified]
401	    all_trades = sum(r.total_trades for r in oos_results)
402	
403	    pf_ci_lower = bootstrap_pf_ci_lower(oos_pfs) if oos_pfs else 0.0
404	    p_edge = float(sum(1 for pf in oos_pfs if pf > 1.0) / max(1, len(oos_pfs)))
405	    mc_95th_dd = float(np.percentile(oos_dds, 95.0)) if oos_dds else 1.0
406	    mean_sharpe = float(np.mean(oos_sharpes)) if oos_sharpes else 0.0
407	    n_obs = max(all_trades, 30)
408	
409	    dsr_raw = deflated_sharpe_ratio(sharpe=mean_sharpe, n_trials=n_grid_combos, n_obs=n_obs)
410	    dsr = dsr_raw.get("dsr", 0.0) if isinstance(dsr_raw, dict) else float(dsr_raw)
411	
412	    wfo_consistency = classify_wfo_consistency(oos_pfs)
413	    fixed_min_pf = fixed_params_metrics.get("fixed_params_min_pf", 0.0)

415	    cost_tier_idx = COST_TIER_ORDER.index(cost_via) if cost_via in COST_TIER_ORDER else -1
416	    cost_passes = cost_tier_idx >= COST_TIER_ORDER.index("realistic")
417	
418	    core_pass = (

427	        and fixed_min_pf >= GATE_FIXED_PARAMS_MIN_PF
428	        and cost_passes

430	    )

434	    elif alt_pass:
435	        verdict, passed_via = "PASS", "alt"
436	    else:
437	        verdict, passed_via = "FAIL", None
438

## [1024] 🤖 ASSISTANT  ·  `2026-06-26T09:19:17.182Z`

This is the honest picture, and it's good news for harness validity plus two real findings:

**The harness is sound** — `load_bars` correctly loaded all 8,407 SPY daily bars (1993→2026); signals are varied; the one survivor (SPY 1h bollinger) got a real gate verdict, correctly FAILed on PBO 0.53 (overfit) + p_edge 0.62. The 33yr SPY "15 trades" is *correct*: a 60/200 SMA cross only fires ~15 times in 33 years (bias is STRONG_BULL for 6,311 bars, but `ENTRY_NOW` only at the cross). MES 1d = 654 bars only (futures daily history is shallow) → 2 crosses → data-starved, not a bug.

**Two real harness flaws the pilot surfaced (exactly its job):**
- **(A) The smoke trade-floor of 30 wrongly kills low-frequency profitable strategies.** SPY 1d sma_trend is profitable pre-cost (PF 1.80, Sharpe 3.13) but has only 15 entries — that's the *nature* of a daily cross, not absence of edge. Killing on trade-count conflates "low frequency" with "no edge."
- **(B) Futures-daily is too shallow** for long-lookback strategies (MES 1d = 2.5yr); deep daily history lives in the ETF proxies. Daily trend belongs on SPY, intraday on MES.

Fix (A) is unambiguously my own bug — fixing it is part of validating the harness, not scaling. Let me also quickly resolve (C): MES 1d adx_ema had 25 entries but 0 executed trades — if that's a sizing bug it'd bite MES intraday at scale too:

## [1050] 🤖 ASSISTANT  ·  `2026-06-26T09:23:46.641Z`

The smoke fix worked — sma_trend SPY 1d now **passes smoke** (was wrongly killed). But it then hit a deeper issue: robustness FAILed with *"insufficient data for WFO windows"* on 33 years of SPY daily data. That's the real root cause, and it's important:

**The WFO geometry is intraday-shaped.** Train 6mo / **test 1mo** / min 30 bars — on *daily* data a 1-month test window is only ~21 bars (< 30), so **no window ever forms**. Daily strategies literally cannot be evaluated by the current gauntlet. And going deeper: a 60/200 daily cross fires ~2 entries/year, so even year-sized windows would be too trade-sparse for per-window WFO — low-frequency daily strategies fundamentally need a *different evaluation mode* (single chronological split + DSR/bootstrap), not many-window walk-forward.

This is a genuine architecture fork, which is exactly the "review before scaling" gate. Let me commit the solid, tested progress first, then lay out the decision for you.

## What's built and tested
The factory foundation is real and green — **26 tests, ruff clean**, on branch `feat/strategy-factory` (commits `6fedc61`, `e3eac03`, `d469957`, `511487c`):

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `pbo.py` | Probability of Backtest Overfitting (CSCV, López de Prado) |
| `purged_kfold.py` | Purged k-fold + embargo (leakage control) |
| `strategy_card.py` | Hypothesis schema + **economic-rationale gate** (kills un-motivated cards) |
| `signal_adapter.py` | One calling convention for every generator |
| `results_db.py` | SQLite audit trail + **global trial counter** (honest DSR denominator) |
| `funnel.py` | smoke → robustness (WFO → shared `compute_gate_v2` + PBO + globally-deflated Sharpe) |
| `orchestrator.py` + `run_pilot.py` | cards → funnel → DB → markdown report |

## What the pilot actually proved (ES/MES + SPY, 1h + 1d)
**The intraday path is validated end-to-end.** Of 10 candidates, the machinery correctly loaded data (full 8,407-row SPY daily back to 1993), generated varied signals, and ran real backtests. The one intraday survivor — SPY-1h Bollinger/RSI — got a **correct robustness FAIL**: PBO 0.53 (overfit), p_edge 0.62, DSR 0.00. That's the system working: a plausible in-sample winner killed by the overfitting tests. Global DSR n_trials = 44 wired through.

**Two real findings the pilot surfaced (its whole purpose):**
- **(A) Fixed** — the smoke trade-floor was killing low-frequency *profitable* strategies (SPY-1d SMA cross: PF 1.80, but only ~15 entries in 33yr because that's how often a 60/200 cross fires). Now flagged `low_sample` and passed through. Regression-tested.
- **(B) Open — your call** — the WFO gauntlet is **intraday-shaped**: a 1-month test window is ~21 daily bars (< 30 min), so *no daily strategy can form windows at all*. Deeper still: a daily trend strategy fires ~2 trades/year, so even year-sized windows are too trade-sparse for per-window walk-forward. Low-frequency daily strategies fundamentally need a **different evaluation mode** (single chronological split + DSR/bootstrap), not many-window WFO.

The honest read: **the factory's WFO+PBO+gate-v2 machinery is the right tool for intraday. Daily/calendar low-frequency edges are a different evaluation regime** — and you *already* have a dedicated, working track for those (the pre-holiday / turn-of-month discovery on deep ETF dailies).

This is the "review before scaling" gate. One decision drives the next move:

1	"""
2	Donchian Channel Breakout signal generator for JARVIS TRADER.
3	
4	Entry : close > highest_high over lookback_entry prior bars (breakout up) — LONG only.
5	Exit  : close < lowest_low over lookback_exit prior bars  OR  ATR trailing stop hit.
6	Stop  : entry - atr_trail_mult × ATR(14) at entry bar.
7	Targets: entry + N × ATR matching trend_signals.py conventions (_T1_MULT=3, _T2=5, _T3=7).
8	
9	Rationale: Donchian captures actual N-bar price highs (no lag like SMA(200)).
10	Compared to SMA(50,200), Donchian enters faster when price breaks a new high,
11	and exits faster on channel breach — both strategies are trend-following but
12	disagree at turning points, making them complementary candidates.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import numpy as np
18	import pandas as pd
19	
20	_ATR_PERIOD = 14
21	_T1_MULT = 3.0
22	_T2_MULT = 5.0
23	_T3_MULT = 7.0
24	
25	
26	def _wilder_atr(high: pd.Series, low: pd.Series, close: pd.Series, period: int = 14) -> pd.Series:
27	    prev_c = close.shift(1)
28	    tr = pd.concat([(high - low), (high - prev_c).abs(), (low - prev_c).abs()], axis=1).max(axis=1)
29	    return tr.ewm(alpha=1 / period, min_periods=period, adjust=False).mean()
30	
31	
32	def generate_donchian_signals(
33	    df: pd.DataFrame,
34	    lookback_entry: int = 20,
35	    lookback_exit: int = 10,
36	    atr_trail_mult: float = 2.0,
37	) -> pd.DataFrame:
38	    """
39	    Generate Donchian Channel breakout signals compatible with the JARVIS Backtester.
40	
41	    Args:
42	        lookback_entry : bars to look back for the channel high (entry condition)
43	        lookback_exit  : bars to look back for the channel low (exit condition)
44	        atr_trail_mult : ATR multiplier for stop and target sizing
45	
46	    Returns df with columns matching trend_signals.py output:
47	        entry_signal  : "ENTRY_NOW" | "NO_TRADE"
48	        exit_signal   : "EXIT_NOW" | "NO_EXIT"
49	        stop_level    : entry − trail_mult × ATR
50	        target_1/2/3  : entry + N × ATR
51	        bias          : "STRONG_BULL" | "NEUTRAL"
52	        regime        : "TRENDING_BULL" | "RANGE_BOUND"
53	        atr           : ATR(14) series
54	    """
55	    df = df.copy()
56	
57	    # Donchian channels (use shift(1) to avoid look-ahead: signal uses yesterday's channel)
58	    channel_high = df["high"].rolling(lookback_entry).max().shift(1)
59	    channel_low = df["low"].rolling(lookback_exit).min().shift(1)
60	    atr = _wilder_atr(df["high"], df["low"], df["close"], _ATR_PERIOD)
61	
62	    # Entry: close breaks above prior N-bar high. Exit: close breaks below prior M-bar low.
63	    in_channel = df["close"] > channel_high  # True when price is above entry channel
64	    breakout_up = in_channel & ~in_channel.shift(1, fill_value=False) & channel_high.notna()
65	    breakdown = df["close"] < channel_low
66	
67	    n = len(df)
68	    entry_signal = np.full(n, "NO_TRADE", dtype=object)
69	    exit_signal  = np.full(n, "NO_EXIT",  dtype=object)
70	    stop_level   = np.full(n, np.nan)
71	    target_1     = np.full(n, np.nan)
72	    target_2     = np.full(n, np.nan)
73	    target_3     = np.full(n, np.nan)
74	
75	    for i in range(n):
76	        if pd.isna(channel_high.iloc[i]) or pd.isna(atr.iloc[i]):
77	            continue
78	        price = float(df["close"].iloc[i])
79	        atr_i = float(atr.iloc[i])
80	
81	        if breakout_up.iloc[i]:
82	            entry_signal[i] = "ENTRY_NOW"
83	            stop_level[i]   = price - atr_trail_mult * atr_i
84	            target_1[i]     = price + _T1_MULT * atr_i
85	            target_2[i]     = price + _T2_MULT * atr_i
86	            target_3[i]     = price + _T3_MULT * atr_i
87	        elif breakdown.iloc[i] and not pd.isna(channel_low.iloc[i]):
88	            exit_signal[i] = "EXIT_NOW"
89	
90	    df["entry_signal"] = entry_signal
91	    df["exit_signal"]  = exit_signal
92	    df["stop_level"]   = stop_level
93	    df["target_1"]     = target_1
94	    df["target_2"]     = target_2
95	    df["target_3"]     = target_3
96	    df["atr"]          = atr
97	
98	    df["bias"] = "NEUTRAL"
99	    df.loc[in_channel & channel_high.notna(), "bias"] = "STRONG_BULL"
100	
101	    df["regime"] = "RANGE_BOUND"
102	    df.loc[in_channel & channel_high.notna(), "regime"] = "TRENDING_BULL"
103	
104	    return df
105	
```

{
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\mattm\\ThinkorSwim\\jarvis-trader\\engine\\backtest\\range_expansion_signals.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Range-expansion breakout signal generator for JARVIS TRADER.\n\nIdea (sourced from an X bookmark @onlybreakouts -- \"the best indicator across\n4,115 strategies ... bar range relative to ATR\", tested across 3,500 NASDAQ\nnames): a bar whose true range is large relative to ATR marks a volatility\nexpansion. When that expansion bar also closes near its extreme, it signals\ndirectional conviction -- momentum that tends to continue on the next bars.\n\nEntry : bar_range = high-low > range_mult x ATR(14)  AND  close in the top\n        (long) / bottom (short) `close_frac` of the bar's range.\nStop  : entry -/+ stop_atr_mult x ATR.\nTargets: entry +/- N x ATR (N = 3/5/7, matching the trend/donchian convention).\n\nLong-and-short. Contract matches generate_donchian_signals so it plugs straight\ninto the Backtester via the factory signal adapter.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\n_ATR_PERIOD = 14\n_T1_MULT = 3.0\n_T2_MULT = 5.0\n_T3_MULT = 7.0\n\n\ndef _wilder_atr(high: pd.Series, low: pd.Series, close: pd.Series, period: int = 14) -> pd.Series:\n    prev_c = close.shift(1)\n    tr = pd.concat([(high - low), (high - prev_c).abs(), (low - prev_c).abs()], axis=1).max(axis=1)\n    return tr.ewm(alpha=1 / period, min_periods=period, adjust=False).mean()\n\n\ndef generate_range_expansion_signals(\n    df: pd.DataFrame,\n    range_mult: float = 1.5,\n    close_frac: float = 0.66,\n    stop_atr_mult: float = 1.5,\n    signal_direction: str = \"both\",\n) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Generate range-expansion momentum signals compatible with the Backtester.\n\n    Args:\n        range_mult: bar true range must exceed this multiple of ATR to qualify.\n        close_frac: close must sit in the top `close_frac` of the bar range for a\n            long (or bottom `close_frac` for a short). 0.66 = upper/lower third.\n        stop_atr_mult: stop distance in ATR multiples.\n        signal_direction: \"long\", \"short\", or \"both\".\n\n    Returns df with entry_signal/exit_signal/stop_level/target_1..3/bias/regime/atr.\n    \"\"\"\n    df = df.copy()\n    high, low, close = df[\"high\"], df[\"low\"], df[\"close\"]\n    atr = _wilder_atr(high, low, close, _ATR_PERIOD)\n\n    bar_range = (high - low).replace(0, np.nan)\n    expansion = bar_range > (range_mult * atr)\n    # Where in the bar did we close? 1.0 = at the high, 0.0 = at the low.\n    close_pos = (close - low) / bar_range\n    want_long = signal_direction in (\"both\", \"long\")\n    want_short = signal_direction in (\"both\", \"short\")\n    long_sig = expansion & (close_pos >= close_frac) & atr.notna()\n    short_sig = expansion & (close_pos <= (1.0 - close_frac)) & atr.notna()\n\n    n = len(df)\n    entry_signal = np.full(n, \"NO_TRADE\", dtype=object)\n    exit_signal = np.full(n, \"NO_EXIT\", dtype=object)\n    stop_level = np.full(n, np.nan)\n    target_1 = np.full(n, np.nan)\n    target_2 = np.full(n, np.nan)\n    target_3 = np.full(n, np.nan)\n    bias = np.full(n, \"NEUTRAL\", dtype=object)\n    regime = np.full(n, \"RANGE_BOUND\", dtype=object)\n\n    for i in range(n):\n        if pd.isna(atr.iloc[i]) or pd.isna(bar_range.iloc[i]):\n            continue\n        price = float(close.iloc[i])\n        atr_i = float(atr.iloc[i])\n        if want_long and bool(long_sig.iloc[i]):\n            entry_signal[i] = \"ENTRY_NOW\"\n            bias[i], regime[i] = \"STRONG_BULL\", \"TRENDING_BULL\"\n            stop_level[i] = price - stop_atr_mult * atr_i\n            target_1[i] = price + _T1_MULT * atr_i\n            target_2[i] = price + _T2_MULT * atr_i\n            target_3[i] = price + _T3_MULT * atr_i\n        elif want_short and bool(short_sig.iloc[i]):\n            entry_signal[i] = \"ENTRY_NOW\"\n            bias[i], regime[i] = \"STRONG_BEAR\", \"TRENDING_BEAR\"\n            stop_level[i] = price + stop_atr_mult * atr_i\n            target_1[i] = price - _T1_MULT * atr_i\n            target_2[i] = price - _T2_MULT * atr_i\n            target_3[i] = price - _T3_MULT * atr_i\n\n    df[\"entry_signal\"] = entry_signal\n    df[\"exit_signal\"] = exit_signal\n    df[\"stop_level\"] = stop_level\n    df[\"target_1\"] = target_1\n    df[\"target_2\"] = target_2\n    df[\"target_3\"] = target_3\n    df[\"bias\"] = bias\n    df[\"regime\"] = regime\n    df[\"atr\"] = atr\n    return df\n"
}

  "content": "---\nname: strategy-factory\ndescription: Hypothesis-first intraday strategy discovery for JARVIS TRADER. Use when asked to discover, scan, or hunt for new intraday trading edges, test a strategy idea across instruments/timeframes, run \"the strategy factory\", or systematically backtest many setups while controlling for overfitting. Runs every economically-motivated candidate through a smoke -> robustness funnel on the existing backtest engine with López de Prado rigor (PBO, purged k-fold, deflated Sharpe with a global trial counter, gate-v2). Intraday only; daily/low-frequency calendar edges belong to the separate calendar track.\n---\n\n# Strategy Factory\n\nDiscover intraday edges the honest way: many candidates is a STATISTICAL hazard\n(test enough noise and lucky winners appear), not a token-cost one (Python\nbacktests are ~free). So shrink the search by **economic rationale**, brute-force\nthe compute, and correct for multiple testing. Passing the factory is NOT an edge\n— it earns a forward-shadow slot, nothing more.\n\nAnnounce: \"Using strategy-factory to scan intraday edges with overfitting control.\"\n\n## Where the code lives\n\n`jarvis-trader/engine/backtest/factory/` (branch `feat/strategy-factory` until\nmerged). Run everything from `engine/` with the engine venv\n(`engine/.venv/Scripts/python.exe`). A throwaway `API_KEY` env var is required\nbecause `Backtester` imports `config` which fail-fasts without it.\n\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `strategy_card.py` | Hypothesis schema + economic-rationale gate |\n| `signal_adapter.py` | One calling convention for every `generate_*_signals` |\n| `data.py` | `load_bars` (end-date-keyed cache), `CONTRACT_SPECS`, `has_cache` |\n| `funnel.py` | `smoke_test` + `robustness_gauntlet` |\n| `pbo.py` / `purged_kfold.py` | Overfitting + leakage control |\n| `results_db.py` | SQLite audit trail + global trial counter |\n| `orchestrator.py` | `factory_cards()`, `run_funnel`, `render_report` |\n| `run_pilot.py` | CLI entry (`--cardset {pilot,factory}`) |\n\n## The 4-phase funnel\n\nEach phase kills cheaply so cognition is spent only on survivors.\n\n### Phase 1 — Strategy Cards (rationale gate)\n\nEvery candidate is a `StrategyCard`: name, family, `signal_ref` (`module:function`),\nentry, exit, **economic_rationale**, native_instruments, native_timeframes,\ndefault_params, param_grid. The gate **kills any card whose rationale is blank or\n< 25 chars** — pre-registration prevents p-hacking. Families: trend, meanrev,\nbreakout, relative_value, calendar, breadth.\n\n### Phase 2 — Smoke (cheap)\n\nOne full-sample backtest per candidate on its native instrument+timeframe, default\nparams. Kill if pre-cost Sharpe < 0.5 or PF < 1.0, or it dies under realistic cost.\n**Do NOT kill on low trade count** — a low-frequency strategy (e.g. a daily cross)\nis flagged `low_sample` and passed through; the bootstrap PF-CI + DSR downstream\nprice in small-sample uncertainty. (Only < 5 trades is killed — nothing to judge.)\n\n### Phase 3 — Robustness gauntlet (the real work; survivors only)\n\nWalk-forward (train 6mo / test 1mo / step 1mo on intraday), IS grid search → OOS,\nfed into the shared `compute_gate_v2`. Then:\n- **PBO** (Probability of Backtest Overfitting, CSCV) across windows — > 0.5 means\n  the in-sample ranking is noise; kill.\n- **Deflated Sharpe** deflated by the **GLOBAL** trial count (every parameterization\n  the whole run tried, fixed before pass 2), not just this card's grid.\n- gate-v2 dual path: core (pf_ci_lower ≥ 1.10, p_edge ≥ 0.95, mc_dd ≤ 5%, dsr ≥ 0.10)\n  or ALT (dsr ≥ 0.30, wfo MODERATE/STRONG, fixed_min_pf ≥ 1.20, cost survives\n  realistic, mc_dd ≤ 4%).\n\n### Phase 4 — Combinations (only Phase-3 survivors)\n\nPairwise ensembles **only between survivors with return correlation < 0.3**\n(uncorrelated = real portfolio edge). Test as a weighted/vote ensemble, not \"if\nboth fire\", and measure each strategy's marginal OOS contribution. (Layer this\nafter at least one survivor exists.)\n\n## Scope: intraday only\n\nThe factory's WFO+PBO machinery fits intraday (1h/30m/15m/5m). **Daily /\nlow-frequency edges go to the calendar track** (turn-of-month, pre-holiday on deep\nETF dailies), where a single chronological split + DSR fits low trade counts — a\n1-month WFO test window is only ~21 daily bars, too few for per-window walk-forward.\n\nUniverse (`FACTORY_INSTRUMENTS`): MES/ES, MNQ/NQ, M2K, MGC/GC, MCL/CL, SPY, QQQ,\nIWM, DIA, GLD, ZB, ZN. `has_cache` skips combos with no data so the DSR denominator\nisn't inflated.\n\n## How to run\n\n```bash\ncd jarvis-trader/engine\nexport API_KEY=\"factory-dummy\"   # throwaway; never the live key\n# Full intraday scan, all instruments, 1h:\n.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m backtest.factory.run_pilot \\\n    --cardset factory --timeframes 1h --out <out_dir>\n# Narrow validation set:\n.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m backtest.factory.run_pilot \\\n    --cardset pilot --instruments MES,SPY --timeframes 1h --out <out_dir>\n```\n\nOutput: `<out_dir>/factory_report.md` (survivors → robustness table → kill reasons\n→ coverage gaps) and `factory_results.sqlite` (full audit). Layer timeframes by\nre-running with `--timeframes 30m` etc. (5m/15m history starts ~2025 → label those\nresults regime-limited). Wall clock ≈ tens of minutes for 1h × full universe; most\ncandidates die at smoke in seconds, survivors take ~30–90s each.\n\n## Adding a new strategy\n\n1. Write a `generate_<name>_signals(df, **params)` in `engine/backtest/` that emits\n   the contract: `entry_signal` (\"ENTRY_NOW\"/\"NO_TRADE\"), `bias`\n   (\"STRONG_BULL\"/\"STRONG_BEAR\"/\"NEUTRAL\"), `stop_level`, `target_1`. Mirror\n   `donchian_signals.py` (LONG) or `range_expansion_signals.py` (long+short). Shift\n   indicators to avoid look-ahead.\n2. Probe it on real bars: `build_signal_frame(ref, load_bars(\"MES\",\"1h\",cache), {})`\n   — confirm it emits the contract and fires a sane number of entries.\n3. Add a `StrategyCard` to `factory_cards()` with a real rationale and a small grid.\n4. TDD the generator (contract + directional firing + calm-bars-don't-fire).\n\nExcluded generators and why: `sma_trend` (daily → calendar), `composite_v3` (takes\na `symbol` arg the adapter can't thread), `vwap` (needs session anchoring), ORB/TPO\n(dedicated engines, add a bespoke adapter later).\n\n## Honest constraints (do not skip)\n\n- **Passing ≠ edge.** With many trials, passers are expected from noise. The only\n  honest verdict is a **forward-shadow** slot (observe-only, no live orders), the\n  same gate the calendar track uses. Never route a factory survivor to live capital\n  on backtest evidence alone — that's Amo's Tier-3 call.\n- **Log every candidate** to the results DB. No quietly-tiny subset dressed up as\n  comprehensive; the DB is the audit trail and the global DSR denominator.\n- **5m/15m data is shallow** (starts ~2025) → those results are regime-limited; the\n  statistical weight is on 1h.\n- **Only real `Backtester.run` output.** No synthetic/estimated metrics. Validate\n  the harness against a known verdict before trusting a scaled run.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Foundation tests: `pytest backtest/factory/ -q` (PBO/purged-kfold known-answers,\n  card gate, adapter, funnel end-to-end, orchestrator).\n- Harness sanity: a smoke survivor must reach a full gate dict (dsr_global, pbo,\n  n_grid_combos); thin data must early-out to FAIL, not crash.\n- Multiple-testing wiring: DSR `n_trials` == global parameterization count, not a\n  single card's grid.\n"
}
```

{

  "content": "\"\"\"Relative-value (pairs) module for the strategy factory.\n\nThe intraday-directional factory is exhausted (660 parameterizations, 0 survivors).\nRelative-value is a STRUCTURALLY different class: mean reversion on a *spread*\nbetween two correlated instruments, not directional momentum on a price. It reuses\nthe whole rigor stack -- WFO windows, gate-v2, PBO, globally-deflated Sharpe -- but\nneeds its own spread constructor and a dollar-neutral two-leg backtester.\n\nSpread (no look-ahead, no fitted beta):\n    spread_t = log(close_A_t) - log(close_B_t)        # 1:1 log spread, dollar-neutral\n    z_t      = (spread_t - mean(spread)_{t-1}) / std(spread)_{t-1}   # rolling, shifted\n\nSignal (mean reversion):\n    z <= -entry_z  -> LONG the spread  (buy A, sell B)\n    z >= +entry_z  -> SHORT the spread (sell A, buy B)\n    |z| <= exit_z  -> flatten\n    |z| >= stop_z  -> stop out (spread blew out -- pair may have de-correlated)\n\nPnL per bar in-position = position * d(spread) = position * (ret_A - ret_B), the\ndollar-neutral pairs return. Each round trip pays cost on BOTH legs.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nfrom backtest.factory.funnel import BacktestMetrics\n\nANNUALIZATION = {\"1h\": np.sqrt(252 * 6.5), \"30m\": np.sqrt(252 * 13), \"1d\": np.sqrt(252)}\n\n\ndef build_spread(close_a: pd.Series, close_b: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Align two close series and return a frame with spread + rolling z-score.\n\n    Mean/std are shifted one bar so the z at time t uses only information available\n    BEFORE t (no look-ahead).\n    \"\"\"\n    df = pd.DataFrame({\"a\": close_a, \"b\": close_b}).dropna()\n    spread = np.log(df[\"a\"]) - np.log(df[\"b\"])\n    mean = spread.rolling(window).mean().shift(1)\n    std = spread.rolling(window).std().shift(1)\n    z = (spread - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)\n    return pd.DataFrame({\"spread\": spread, \"z\": z}, index=df.index)\n\n\ndef backtest_spread(\n    close_a: pd.Series,\n    close_b: pd.Series,\n    *,\n    window: int = 60,\n    entry_z: float = 2.0,\n    exit_z: float = 0.5,\n    stop_z: float = 4.0,\n    cost_bps_per_leg: float = 1.0,\n    timeframe: str = \"1h\",\n) -> BacktestMetrics:\n    \"\"\"Vectorized dollar-neutral z-score reversion backtest. Returns BacktestMetrics\n    so the gauntlet can treat it identically to a single-instrument result.\"\"\"\n    sp = build_spread(close_a, close_b, window)\n    spread, z = sp[\"spread\"].to_numpy(), sp[\"z\"].to_numpy()\n    n = len(sp)\n    if n < window + 5:\n        return BacktestMetrics(profit_factor=0.0, sharpe_ratio=0.0, max_drawdown_pct=0.0, total_trades=0)\n\n    d_spread = np.diff(spread, prepend=spread[0])  # bar-over-bar spread change\n    pos = 0  # current position: +1 long spread, -1 short spread, 0 flat\n    cost = cost_bps_per_leg * 2.0 / 1e4  # round-trip cost (both legs) in spread-return units\n    bar_pnl = np.zeros(n)\n    trade_pnls: list[float] = []\n    cur_trade = 0.0\n    n_trades = 0\n\n    for i in range(1, n):\n        zi = z[i]\n        if np.isnan(zi):\n            continue\n        # accrue PnL on the position held into bar i\n        if pos != 0:\n            bar_pnl[i] = pos * d_spread[i]\n            cur_trade += bar_pnl[i]\n        # state transitions (decided on this bar's z, applied to next bar's accrual)\n        if pos == 0:\n            if zi <= -entry_z:\n                pos = 1\n            elif zi >= entry_z:\n                pos = -1\n        else:\n            blew_out = abs(zi) >= stop_z\n            reverted = abs(zi) <= exit_z\n            if reverted or blew_out:\n                cur_trade -= cost  # pay round-trip cost on close\n                trade_pnls.append(cur_trade)\n                n_trades += 1\n                cur_trade = 0.0\n                pos = 0\n    # close any open trade at the end\n    if pos != 0:\n        cur_trade -= cost\n        trade_pnls.append(cur_trade)\n        n_trades += 1\n\n    if n_trades == 0:\n        return BacktestMetrics(profit_factor=0.0, sharpe_ratio=0.0, max_drawdown_pct=0.0, total_trades=0)\n\n    tp = np.array(trade_pnls)\n    gains = tp[tp > 0].sum()\n    losses = -tp[tp < 0].sum()\n    pf = float(gains / losses) if losses > 0 else (5.0 if gains > 0 else 0.0)\n\n    ann = ANNUALIZATION.get(timeframe, np.sqrt(252 * 6.5))\n    active = bar_pnl[bar_pnl != 0.0]\n    sharpe = float(active.mean() / active.std() * ann) if active.size > 1 and active.std() > 0 else 0.0\n\n    equity = np.cumsum(bar_pnl)\n    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)\n    dd = peak - equity\n    # express max drawdown as a fraction of the gross profit scale (spread is unitless)\n    denom = max(abs(equity).max(), 1e-9)\n    max_dd_pct = float(dd.max() / denom * 100.0)\n\n    return BacktestMetrics(\n        profit_factor=pf,\n        sharpe_ratio=sharpe,\n        max_drawdown_pct=max_dd_pct,\n        total_trades=int(n_trades),\n    )\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Tests for the relative-value (pairs) backtester.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\n\nfrom backtest.factory.relval import backtest_spread, build_spread\n\n\ndef _series(arr) -> pd.Series:\n    idx = pd.date_range(\"2025-01-01\", periods=len(arr), freq=\"h\")\n    return pd.Series(arr, index=idx)\n\n\ndef _cointegrated(n=4000, seed=1):\n    \"\"\"B is a random walk; A = B plus a mean-reverting (OU) deviation. So\n    log(A)-log(B) mean-reverts -> z-score reversion should profit.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    common = np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.01, n))\n    ou = np.zeros(n)\n    for t in range(1, n):\n        ou[t] = ou[t - 1] * 0.95 + rng.normal(0, 0.02)  # mean-reverting deviation\n    a = np.exp(common + ou)\n    b = np.exp(common)\n    return _series(a), _series(b)\n\n\ndef _random_walk_pair(n=4000, seed=2):\n    \"\"\"Two independent random walks -> spread is itself a random walk (no reversion).\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    a = np.exp(np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.01, n)))\n    b = np.exp(np.cumsum(rng.normal(0, 0.01, n)))\n    return _series(a), _series(b)\n\n\ndef test_build_spread_no_lookahead():\n    a, b = _cointegrated(500)\n    sp = build_spread(a, b, window=60)\n    # first `window` z-values must be NaN (rolling+shift warm-up) -> no peeking\n    assert sp[\"z\"].iloc[:60].isna().all()\n    assert sp[\"z\"].iloc[100:].notna().any()\n\n\ndef test_cointegrated_pair_is_profitable():\n    a, b = _cointegrated()\n    m = backtest_spread(a, b, window=60, entry_z=2.0, exit_z=0.5, cost_bps_per_leg=0.5)\n    assert m.total_trades >= 10\n    assert m.profit_factor > 1.2, f\"reversion edge should be profitable, got pf={m.profit_factor}\"\n\n\ndef test_random_walk_pair_has_no_edge():\n    a, b = _random_walk_pair()\n    m = backtest_spread(a, b, window=60, entry_z=2.0, exit_z=0.5, cost_bps_per_leg=1.0)\n    # no genuine reversion -> profit factor should not show a real edge\n    assert m.profit_factor < 1.5\n\n\ndef test_returns_metrics_contract():\n    a, b = _cointegrated(1000)\n    m = backtest_spread(a, b)\n    assert hasattr(m, \"profit_factor\") and hasattr(m, \"sharpe_ratio\")\n    assert hasattr(m, \"max_drawdown_pct\") and hasattr(m, \"total_trades\")\n\n\ndef test_thin_data_returns_zero_trades():\n    a, b = _cointegrated(40)\n    m = backtest_spread(a, b, window=60)\n    assert m.total_trades == 0\n"

"Make this into a skill." Strategize optimally first "without reducing the quality, accuracy, or depth."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Backtest overfitting / false discovery (López de Prado):** testing N candidates guarantees lucky winners; core problem the whole campaign hit.
   - **PBO (Probability of Backtest Overfitting)** via CSCV (Combinatorially-Symmetric Cross-Validation).
   - **Purged k-fold CV with embargo** (leakage control).
   - **Deflated Sharpe Ratio** deflated by the GLOBAL trial count (every parameterization the whole run tried, fixed before pass 2).
   - **Economic-rationale gate:** kill cards with blank/<25-char rationale (anti-p-hacking, pre-registration).
   - **gate-v2 dual-path:** core (pf_ci_lower≥1.10, p_edge≥0.95, mc_95th_dd≤5%, dsr≥0.10) OR ALT (dsr≥0.30, wfo MODERATE/STRONG, fixed_params_min_pf≥1.20, cost survives realistic, mc_dd≤4%).

   - **WFO geometry:** train 6mo / test 1mo / step 1mo, MIN_BARS_PER_SPLIT=30 — intraday-shaped (a 1mo test window = ~21 daily bars < 30, so daily strategies can't form windows → daily belongs to calendar track).
   - **Relative-value pairs trading:** spread = log(close_A) - log(close_B) (1:1 log spread, no fitted beta = no look-ahead); z-score with rolling mean/std SHIFTED one bar; mean-reversion entry/exit on z; dollar-neutral PnL = position × Δspread = position × (ret_A − ret_B).

1	"""Relative-value (pairs) module for the strategy factory.
2	
3	The intraday-directional factory is exhausted (660 parameterizations, 0 survivors).
4	Relative-value is a STRUCTURALLY different class: mean reversion on a *spread*
5	between two correlated instruments, not directional momentum on a price. It reuses
6	the whole rigor stack -- WFO windows, gate-v2, PBO, globally-deflated Sharpe -- but
7	needs its own spread constructor and a dollar-neutral two-leg backtester.
8	
9	Spread (no look-ahead, no fitted beta):
10	    spread_t = log(close_A_t) - log(close_B_t)        # 1:1 log spread, dollar-neutral
11	    z_t      = (spread_t - mean(spread)_{t-1}) / std(spread)_{t-1}   # rolling, shifted
12	
13	Signal (mean reversion):
14	    z <= -entry_z  -> LONG the spread  (buy A, sell B)
15	    z >= +entry_z  -> SHORT the spread (sell A, buy B)
16	    |z| <= exit_z  -> flatten
17	    |z| >= stop_z  -> stop out (spread blew out -- pair may have de-correlated)
18	
19	PnL per bar in-position = position * d(spread) = position * (ret_A - ret_B), the
20	dollar-neutral pairs return. Each round trip pays cost on BOTH legs.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
26	from itertools import product
27	
28	import numpy as np
29	import pandas as pd
30	
31	from backtest.deflated_sharpe import deflated_sharpe_ratio
32	from backtest.factory.funnel import (
33	    SMOKE_LOW_SAMPLE_TRADES,
34	    SMOKE_MIN_PF,
35	    SMOKE_MIN_SHARPE,
36	    SMOKE_MIN_TRADES,
37	    BacktestMetrics,
38	    _windows,
39	)
40	from backtest.factory.pbo import probability_of_backtest_overfitting
41	from backtest.wfo_lifecycle import OOSResult, compute_gate_v2
42	
43	ANNUALIZATION = {"1h": np.sqrt(252 * 6.5), "30m": np.sqrt(252 * 13), "1d": np.sqrt(252)}
44	# Realistic round-trip cost per leg (bps). A micro-future round turn ~= 0.5-1 bp.
45	REALISTIC_COST_BPS = 1.0
46	
47	
48	def build_spread(close_a: pd.Series, close_b: pd.Series, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
49	    """Align two close series and return a frame with spread + rolling z-score.
50	
51	    Mean/std are shifted one bar so the z at time t uses only information available
52	    BEFORE t (no look-ahead).
53	    """
54	    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": close_a, "b": close_b}).dropna()
55	    spread = np.log(df["a"]) - np.log(df["b"])
56	    mean = spread.rolling(window).mean().shift(1)
57	    std = spread.rolling(window).std().shift(1)
58	    z = (spread - mean) / std.replace(0, np.nan)
59	    return pd.DataFrame({"spread": spread, "z": z}, index=df.index)
60	
61	
62	def backtest_spread(
63	    close_a: pd.Series,
64	    close_b: pd.Series,
65	    *,
66	    window: int = 60,
67	    entry_z: float = 2.0,
68	    exit_z: float = 0.5,
69	    stop_z: float = 4.0,
70	    cost_bps_per_leg: float = 1.0,
71	    timeframe: str = "1h",
72	) -> BacktestMetrics:
73	    """Vectorized dollar-neutral z-score reversion backtest. Returns BacktestMetrics
74	    so the gauntlet can treat it identically to a single-instrument result."""
75	    sp = build_spread(close_a, close_b, window)
76	    spread, z = sp["spread"].to_numpy(), sp["z"].to_numpy()
77	    n = len(sp)
78	    if n < window + 5:
79	        return BacktestMetrics(
80	            profit_factor=0.0, sharpe_ratio=0.0, max_drawdown_pct=0.0, total_trades=0
81	        )
82	
83	    d_spread = np.diff(spread, prepend=spread[0])  # bar-over-bar spread change
84	    pos = 0  # current position: +1 long spread, -1 short spread, 0 flat
85	    cost = cost_bps_per_leg * 2.0 / 1e4  # round-trip cost (both legs) in spread-return units
86	    bar_pnl = np.zeros(n)
87	    trade_pnls: list[float] = []
88	    cur_trade = 0.0
89	    n_trades = 0
90	
91	    for i in range(1, n):
92	        zi = z[i]
93	        if np.isnan(zi):
94	            continue
95	        # accrue PnL on the position held into bar i
96	        if pos != 0:
97	            bar_pnl[i] = pos * d_spread[i]
98	            cur_trade += bar_pnl[i]
99	        # state transitions (decided on this bar's z, applied to next bar's accrual)
100	        if pos == 0:
101	            if zi <= -entry_z:
102	                pos = 1
103	            elif zi >= entry_z:
104	                pos = -1
105	        else:
106	            blew_out = abs(zi) >= stop_z
107	            reverted = abs(zi) <= exit_z
108	            if reverted or blew_out:
109	                cur_trade -= cost  # pay round-trip cost on close
110	                trade_pnls.append(cur_trade)
111	                n_trades += 1
112	                cur_trade = 0.0
113	                pos = 0
114	    # close any open trade at the end
115	    if pos != 0:
116	        cur_trade -= cost
117	        trade_pnls.append(cur_trade)
118	        n_trades += 1
119	
120	    if n_trades == 0:
121	        return BacktestMetrics(
122	            profit_factor=0.0, sharpe_ratio=0.0, max_drawdown_pct=0.0, total_trades=0
123	        )
124	
125	    tp = np.array(trade_pnls)
126	    gains = tp[tp > 0].sum()
127	    losses = -tp[tp < 0].sum()
128	    pf = float(gains / losses) if losses > 0 else (5.0 if gains > 0 else 0.0)
129	
130	    ann = ANNUALIZATION.get(timeframe, np.sqrt(252 * 6.5))
131	    active = bar_pnl[bar_pnl != 0.0]
132	    sharpe = (
133	        float(active.mean() / active.std() * ann) if active.size > 1 and active.std() > 0 else 0.0
134	    )
135	
136	    equity = np.cumsum(bar_pnl)
137	    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(equity)
138	    dd = peak - equity
139	    # express max drawdown as a fraction of the gross profit scale (spread is unitless)
140	    denom = max(abs(equity).max(), 1e-9)
141	    max_dd_pct = float(dd.max() / denom * 100.0)
142	
143	    return BacktestMetrics(
144	        profit_factor=pf,
145	        sharpe_ratio=sharpe,
146	        max_drawdown_pct=max_dd_pct,
147	        total_trades=int(n_trades),
148	    )

216	            leg_a="ES",
217	            leg_b="NQ",
218	            economic_rationale="Full-size S&P vs Nasdaq -- the deepest, most-arbitraged index "
219	            "cross; the spread mean-reverts around the common market factor on a sector-rotation "
220	            "horizon.",
221	            **common,
222	        ),
223	    ]
224	
225	
226	def _aligned(bars_a: pd.DataFrame, bars_b: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
227	    """Inner-join two bar frames on timestamp -> columns a, b (close prices)."""
228	    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": bars_a["close"], "b": bars_b["close"]}).dropna()
229	    return df
230	
231	
232	def _grid(pair: Pair) -> list[dict]:
233	    if not pair.param_grid:
234	        return [dict(pair.default_params)]
235	    keys = list(pair.param_grid)
236	    return [
237	        {**pair.default_params, **dict(zip(keys, combo, strict=True))}
238	        for combo in product(*(pair.param_grid[k] for k in keys))
239	    ]
240	
241	
242	def smoke_test_pair(
243	    pair: Pair, bars_a: pd.DataFrame, bars_b: pd.DataFrame, timeframe: str
244	) -> tuple[bool, dict]:
245	    """Pre-cost reversion edge, then realistic-cost survival -- mirrors funnel.smoke_test."""
246	    al = _aligned(bars_a, bars_b)
247	    pre = backtest_spread(
248	        al["a"], al["b"], timeframe=timeframe, cost_bps_per_leg=0.0, **pair.default_params
249	    )
250	    low_sample = pre.total_trades < SMOKE_LOW_SAMPLE_TRADES
251	    base = {
252	        "stage": "smoke",
253	        "pre_sharpe": pre.sharpe_ratio,
254	        "pre_pf": pre.profit_factor,
255	        "trades": pre.total_trades,
256	        "low_sample": low_sample,
257	    }
258	    if pre.total_trades < SMOKE_MIN_TRADES:
259	        return False, {
260	            **base,
261	            "kill_reason": f"insufficient trades to evaluate (<{SMOKE_MIN_TRADES})",
262	        }
263	    if pre.sharpe_ratio < SMOKE_MIN_SHARPE or pre.profit_factor < SMOKE_MIN_PF:
264	        return False, {**base, "kill_reason": "pre-cost sharpe/pf below floor"}
265	    post = backtest_spread(
266	        al["a"],
267	        al["b"],
268	        timeframe=timeframe,
269	        cost_bps_per_leg=REALISTIC_COST_BPS,
270	        **pair.default_params,
271	    )
272	    survives = post.profit_factor > SMOKE_MIN_PF
273	    return survives, {
274	        **base,
275	        "post_cost_pf": post.profit_factor,
276	        "post_cost_sharpe": post.sharpe_ratio,
277	        "kill_reason": None if survives else "does not survive realistic cost",
278	    }
279	
280	
281	def relval_gauntlet(
282	    pair: Pair,
283	    bars_a: pd.DataFrame,
284	    bars_b: pd.DataFrame,
285	    timeframe: str,
286	    global_trial_count: int,
287	) -> dict:
288	    """Walk-forward + gate-v2 + PBO + globally-deflated Sharpe for one pair."""
289	    al = _aligned(bars_a, bars_b)
290	    windows = _windows(al)
291	    grid = _grid(pair)
292	    n_combos = len(grid)
293	    if not windows:
294	        return {"verdict": "FAIL", "reason": "insufficient data for WFO windows"}
295	
296	    def _bt(seg: pd.DataFrame, params: dict, cost: float) -> BacktestMetrics:
297	        return backtest_spread(
298	            seg["a"], seg["b"], timeframe=timeframe, cost_bps_per_leg=cost, **params
299	        )
300	
301	    oos_results: list[OOSResult] = []
302	    for win in windows:
303	        tr = al[(al.index >= win["tr_s"]) & (al.index < win["tr_e"])]
304	        te = al[(al.index >= win["te_s"]) & (al.index <= win["te_e"])]
305	        best_pf, best_params = -1.0, None
306	        for params in grid:
307	            m = _bt(tr, params, 0.0)
308	            pf = min(m.profit_factor, 5.0) if np.isfinite(m.profit_factor) else 5.0
309	            if m.total_trades >= 5 and pf > best_pf:
310	                best_pf, best_params = pf, params
311	        if best_params is None:
312	            continue
313	        oos = _bt(te, best_params, REALISTIC_COST_BPS)
314	        oos_results.append(
315	            OOSResult(
316	                window_idx=win["n"],
317	                best_params=best_params,
318	                profit_factor=oos.profit_factor,
319	                max_drawdown_pct=oos.max_drawdown_pct,
320	                sharpe_ratio=oos.sharpe_ratio,
321	                total_trades=oos.total_trades,
322	            )
323	        )
324	    if not oos_results:
325	        return {"verdict": "FAIL", "reason": "no OOS windows produced trades"}
326	
327	    fixed_pfs = []
328	    for params in grid:
329	        m = _bt(al, params, REALISTIC_COST_BPS)
330	        if m.total_trades >= 5 and np.isfinite(m.profit_factor):
331	            fixed_pfs.append(m.profit_factor)
332	    fixed_metrics = {"fixed_params_min_pf": float(min(fixed_pfs)) if fixed_pfs else 0.0}
333	    cost_metrics = {
334	        "cost_survives_through": "realistic" if fixed_pfs and min(fixed_pfs) > 1.0 else "none"
335	    }
336	
337	    gate = compute_gate_v2(oos_results, n_combos, fixed_metrics, cost_metrics)
338	
339	    mean_sharpe = float(np.mean([r.sharpe_ratio for r in oos_results]))
340	    total_oos_trades = sum(r.total_trades for r in oos_results)
341	    dsr_global = deflated_sharpe_ratio(
342	        sharpe=mean_sharpe,
343	        n_trials=max(global_trial_count, n_combos),
344	        n_obs=max(total_oos_trades, 30),
345	    )
346	    dsr_global_val = (
347	        dsr_global.get("dsr", 0.0) if isinstance(dsr_global, dict) else float(dsr_global)
348	    )
349	
350	    pbo_val = None
351	    if len(windows) >= 4 and n_combos >= 2:
352	        rows = []
353	        for win in windows:
354	            seg = al[(al.index >= win["tr_s"]) & (al.index <= win["te_e"])]
355	            rows.append(
356	                [
357	                    (m.profit_factor if np.isfinite(m.profit_factor) else 5.0)
358	                    for m in (_bt(seg, p, 0.0) for p in grid)
359	                ]
360	            )
361	        pf_matrix = np.asarray(rows, dtype=float)
362	        if pf_matrix.shape[0] >= 4:
363	            s = min(pf_matrix.shape[0] - (pf_matrix.shape[0] % 2), 10)
364	            if s >= 2:
365	                pbo_val = probability_of_backtest_overfitting(pf_matrix, n_partitions=s).pbo
366	
367	    gate["dsr_global"] = round(dsr_global_val, 6)
368	    gate["pbo"] = pbo_val
369	    gate["n_grid_combos"] = n_combos
370	    gate["global_trial_count"] = global_trial_count
371	    return gate
372	
```

276	
277	def enumerate_candidates(
278	    cards: list[StrategyCard], universe: Universe
279	) -> list[tuple[StrategyCard, str, str]]:
280	    """Card x (native instruments ∩ universe) x (native timeframes ∩ universe)."""
281	    inst = set(universe.instruments)
282	    tfs = set(universe.timeframes)
283	    out = []
284	    for card in cards:
285	        for sym in [s for s in card.native_instruments if s in inst]:
286	            for tf in [t for t in card.native_timeframes if t in tfs]:
287	                out.append((card, sym, tf))
288	    return out
289	
290	
291	def run_funnel(
292	    cards: list[StrategyCard],
293	    universe: Universe,
294	    cache_dir: str | Path,
295	    db_path: str | Path,
296	    created_at: str,
297	) -> dict:
298	    """Run the full pilot funnel. Returns a summary dict; full detail is in the DB."""
299	    db = ResultsDB(db_path)
300	    run_id = db.new_run(
301	        created_at,
302	        {"universe": vars(universe), "n_cards": len(cards), "cache_dir": str(cache_dir)},
303	    )
304	
305	    all_candidates = enumerate_candidates(cards, universe)
306	    # Drop combos with no cached data BEFORE counting trials, so the global DSR
307	    # denominator reflects only configurations that actually run (no phantom
308	    # inflation from missing instrument/timeframe cells).
309	    candidates = [(c, s, t) for c, s, t in all_candidates if has_cache(s, t, cache_dir)]
310	    skipped = [(c, s, t) for c, s, t in all_candidates if not has_cache(s, t, cache_dir)]
311	    # Global DSR denominator = total parameterizations the factory will try.
312	    global_trials = sum(c.n_param_combos() for c, _, _ in candidates)
313	
314	    rows = []
315	    for card, sym, tf in skipped:
316	        rows.append(
317	            {"card": card.name, "sym": sym, "tf": tf, "stage": "skip", "reason": "no cache"}
318	        )
319	    for card, sym, tf in candidates:
320	        cid = db.record_candidate(run_id, card.name, sym, tf, card.default_params, "smoke")
321	        try:
322	            bars = load_bars(sym, tf, cache_dir)
323	        except FileNotFoundError as e:
324	            db.record_result(cid, "smoke", {"error": str(e)}, verdict="SKIP", kill_reason="no data")
325	            rows.append(
326	                {"card": card.name, "sym": sym, "tf": tf, "stage": "skip", "reason": "no data"}
327	            )
328	            continue
329	        mult = float(spec_for(sym)["multiplier"])
330	
331	        survives, sm = smoke_test(card, bars, sym, mult)
332	        db.record_result(
333	            cid,
334	            "smoke",
335	            sm,
336	            verdict="PASS" if survives else "KILL",
337	            kill_reason=sm.get("kill_reason"),
338	        )
339	        row = {"card": card.name, "sym": sym, "tf": tf, "smoke": sm, "smoke_pass": survives}
340	        if not survives:
341	            row["stage"] = "killed_smoke"
342	            rows.append(row)
343	            continue
344	
345	        gate = robustness_gauntlet(card, bars, sym, mult, global_trials)

20	    "ES": {"multiplier": 50.0, "tick": 0.25},
21	    "MNQ": {"multiplier": 2.0, "tick": 0.25},

26	    "MCL": {"multiplier": 100.0, "tick": 0.01},
27	    "CL": {"multiplier": 1000.0, "tick": 0.01},
28	    "ZB": {"multiplier": 1000.0, "tick": 0.03125},
29	    "ZN": {"multiplier": 1000.0, "tick": 0.015625},
30	    # ETFs trade 1 share-equivalent; multiplier 1, penny tick.
31	    "SPY": {"multiplier": 1.0, "tick": 0.01},
32	    "QQQ": {"multiplier": 1.0, "tick": 0.01},
33	    "IWM": {"multiplier": 1.0, "tick": 0.01},
34	    "DIA": {"multiplier": 1.0, "tick": 0.01},
35	    "GLD": {"multiplier": 1.0, "tick": 0.01},
36	}
37	
38	# Cache uses MES_F / ES_F style prefixes for some symbols; map symbol -> prefix.
39	_PREFIX_OVERRIDE = {"ES": "ES_F"}
40	
41	
42	def load_bars(
43	    symbol: str,
44	    timeframe: str,
45	    cache_dir: str | Path,
46	    *,
47	    tz: str = "America/New_York",
48	) -> pd.DataFrame:
49	    """Load the freshest cached bars for `symbol` at `timeframe`.
50	
51	    Returns an OHLC(V) frame indexed by tz-aware DatetimeIndex, ascending.
52	    """
53	    cache_dir = Path(cache_dir)
54	    prefix = _PREFIX_OVERRIDE.get(symbol, symbol)
55	    path = _find_latest_cache(cache_dir, prefix, suffix=f"_{timeframe}.csv")
56	
57	    df = pd.read_csv(path)
58	    df.columns = [c.lower() for c in df.columns]
59	    ts_col = "timestamp" if "timestamp" in df.columns else "datetime"
60	    ts = pd.to_datetime(df[ts_col])
61	    if ts.dt.tz is None:
62	        ts = ts.dt.tz_localize("UTC").dt.tz_convert(tz)
63	    df[ts_col] = ts
64	    df = df.set_index(ts_col).sort_index()
65	
66	    required = {"open", "high", "low", "close"}
67	    missing = required - set(df.columns)
68	    if missing:
69	        raise ValueError(f"{path.name} missing columns: {missing}")
70	    return df
71	
72	
73	def spec_for(symbol: str) -> dict:
74	    if symbol not in CONTRACT_SPECS:
75	        raise KeyError(f"no contract spec for '{symbol}' -- add it to CONTRACT_SPECS")
76	    return CONTRACT_SPECS[symbol]
77	
78	
79	def has_cache(symbol: str, timeframe: str, cache_dir: str | Path) -> bool:
80	    """True if at least one cache file exists for symbol+timeframe (no read)."""
81	    prefix = _PREFIX_OVERRIDE.get(symbol, symbol)
82	    return any(Path(cache_dir).glob(f"{prefix}_*_{timeframe}.csv"))

177	
178	    where ``<START_DATE>`` and ``<END_DATE>`` are ISO ``YYYY-MM-DD`` strings.
179	    Lexicographic max on the second underscore-split segment (``parts[2]``,
180	    the end-date) is equivalent to chronological max because ISO dates sort
181	    correctly as strings. ``parts[0]`` is the prefix, ``parts[1]`` is the
182	    start-date, ``parts[2]`` is the end-date — the sort key.
183	
184	    A refreshed IBKR pull (e.g. ``MES_2024-01-01_2026-05-07_1h.csv``) will
185	    therefore always win over an older copy (e.g.

188	    silently revert to a hardcoded path.
189	
190	    Contract drift policy: filenames matching the glob ``<prefix>*<suffix>``
191	    but violating the underscore-split contract (fewer than 3 segments) sort
192	    to the empty string and end up at the bottom of the lex order, so they
193	    never beat a contract-conforming sibling. They will only be selected if
194	    no conforming file exists, in which case the helper falls back to the
195	    glob-sort tail and a warning is logged. The companion runtime assertion
